title: Preeclampsia / Eclampsia / HELLP
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Preeclampsia / Eclampsia / HELLP (ACOG 2024)
ACOG Practice Bulletin on gestational hypertension and preeclampsia; AHA OBLS 2024; Tennessee HELLP criteria (Sibai)

changelog.change: Initial entry — diagnostic criteria + severe features, the severe-hypertension treatment table, the full magnesium protocol (loading / maintenance / monitoring / antidote), and HELLP with delivery timing.

summary: Severe-range BP (SBP ≥ 160 or DBP ≥ 110, sustained) must be treated within 15–60 minutes to prevent haemorrhagic stroke — target 140–155 / 90–105. Magnesium sulfate is for seizure prophylaxis and treatment, NOT for blood pressure. Definitive treatment is delivery.

items: SBP ≥ 140 OR DBP ≥ 90 on two occasions ≥ 4 h apart, PLUS proteinuria (≥ 300 mg/24 h, P:Cr ≥ 0.3, or dipstick ≥ 2+),
OR — without proteinuria — any of: thrombocytopenia, renal insufficiency, transaminitis, pulmonary oedema, new headache, or visual disturbance.
SBP ≥ 160 or DBP ≥ 110 (sustained on two readings ≥ 4 h apart, or once if antihypertensive already started).
Creatinine > 1.1 mg/dL or doubling of baseline.
AST/ALT > 2× ULN, ± RUQ / epigastric pain (suggests HELLP).
New headache unresponsive to medication, or visual disturbance.

rows: Onset ~5 min. Avoid in asthma / severe bradycardia / decompensated HF
5–10 mg IV q20 min, max ~20 mg
Onset 10–20 min; more maternal hypotension — have fluids + fetal monitoring ready
10–20 mg PO q20 min, max 50 mg/hr
Preferred when no IV access. Compatible with magnesium (the old neuromuscular-blockade concern wasn't borne out)

body.text: Target 140–155 / 90–105 mmHg — avoid over-correction (uteroplacental insufficiency, fetal distress).

rows: 6 g IV over 15–20 min (OBLS); 4–6 g if for prophylaxis only
Hourly: deep tendon reflexes (absent → STOP), respiratory rate (≥ 12/min), urine output (≥ 25 mL/hr)
Loss of DTRs ~ 7–10 mEq/L (stop the infusion); respiratory depression ~ 12–15 mEq/L; cardiac arrest higher
Calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 3 min
Continue for 24 h after delivery OR after the last seizure
Give the load, then reduce or hold the maintenance and follow levels — magnesium is renally cleared

body.text: Eclamptic seizure: most are self-limited — protect the airway, left lateral, O2, and give / continue magnesium (a bolus of 2–4 g IV over 5 min for a breakthrough seizure on the infusion). Magnesium is superior to phenytoin AND benzodiazepines for eclampsia. Persistent seizures despite magnesium → a benzodiazepine, then levetiracetam / fosphenytoin, and reconsider the differential (intracranial haemorrhage, PRES, other).

items: Tennessee criteria — Haemolysis (LDH > 600 U/L, schistocytes, bilirubin > 1.2 mg/dL) + Elevated Liver enzymes (AST/ALT > 2× ULN) + Low Platelets (< 100,000). 'Partial' HELLP has one or two of the three.
Can occur with only mildly elevated BP or none. RUQ / epigastric pain, nausea, malaise. Watch for hepatic haematoma / rupture, abruption, DIC, AKI.

Delivery: promptly after maternal stabilisation if ≥ 34 weeks, or at any gestation if maternal or fetal condition is deteriorating (DIC, hepatic infarct/haematoma, abruption, non-reassuring fetal status, uncontrollable severe hypertension).

< 34 weeks and stable: a short course of antenatal corticosteroids + magnesium, then deliver. Steroids improve fetal lung maturity — the transient platelet bump is not a reason to delay delivery when indicated.
Platelet transfusion: for platelets < 20,000, or < 50,000 with active bleeding or before a caesarean.
